inputs.text: This public apology is understandable, but it risks turning a budget crisis into a story about ordinary parents feeling guilty while the people controlling the system escape scrutiny. Another shortfall and more than 70 school positions on the chopping block are being presented as unavoidable—as if there’s no choice but to make educators and students pay. I don’t buy that framing. Repeated “shortfalls” can serve as cover for priorities being set out of sight, while the public is encouraged to apologize instead of asking who benefits from keeping schools in crisis.
